get.description:
Exchanges authorization code for tokens and sets access token cookie.

Query Parameters:     code: Authorization code from OIDC provider     state: CSRF token from OIDC provider

Returns:     302: Redirect to original redirect URL with access token cookie set     400: Invalid or missing callback parameters     401: Token exchange failed
get.summary: Handle OIDC callback after user authorization.

get.description:
Generates authorization URL and redirects to OIDC provider. PKCE state is encrypted into the OAuth state parameter. The ``redirect_uri`` is the callback on the origin the request came in on, so the app signs in on every hostname it is served on (each one registered at the IdP).

Query Parameters:     redirect: Path to redirect to after successful login (required)

Returns:     302: Redirect to OIDC provider authorization endpoint     400: Missing or invalid redirect parameter
get.summary: Initiate OIDC login flow with PKCE.

get.description:
Clears access token cookie and redirects to OIDC provider's logout endpoint to terminate the session at the IdP level.

Query Parameters:     redirect: Path to redirect to after logout (default: /)

Returns:     302: Redirect to OIDC logout endpoint (or direct redirect if OIDC disabled)     400: Invalid redirect parameter
get.summary: Log out current user.

get.description:
This endpoint is @public, so the request hook resolves the caller (refreshing an expired access token) without answering 401 itself, and the handler answers 401 when no one is signed in. A caller with none of the app's roles gets 403 from the hook. With OIDC disabled, the caller is the local admin.

Returns:     200: User information     401: No valid token provided or token invalid     403: User authenticated but has none of the app's roles
get.summary: Get current authenticated user information.

post.summary: The hook's check of a file of the store's tree after an edit (design 1 §5.6 step 3): the file's hash on disk, once its sidecar has it acked, in; whether the server agrees with it, every Save Error of the store's tree and every deferral without a home out. A `reverted` Save Error is answered once and deleted; a `parse` one stands until a clean save of its path.

get.description: `hello` first, `{protocol: {min, max}, manifest_hash}`; then a `change`, `{path, hash}`, for every tree hash that moved once its transaction has committed, and a `manifest`, `{}`, whenever the set of syncing projects changed; a heartbeat comment after `SYNC_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` idle. No `id:` field: the sidecar's hashes are its cursor. Ends on shutdown, and when the stream falls too far behind. Refused with 401, 403 or 426 as every sync call is.
get.summary: The store's change stream (design 1 §5.4): `text/event-stream`.
The bytes a file of the store's tree must hold, with their hash as `X-Pilot-Hash`. 404 for a path of no syncing project.

put.description:
Headers: `X-Pilot-Base-Hash`, the hash the sidecar last synced for the path, or `none`. The body is the file's bytes, at most `SYNC_PUT_MAX_BYTES`.

Answers 204 when the file needs no change, 200 with the bytes it must now hold when it does; either with `X-Pilot-Hash`, the hash the file holds once answered, and `X-Pilot-Faults`, the count of Save Errors the save raised on the path, and `X-Pilot-Stale: true` when the base hash was not the path's tree hash. 404 for a path of no syncing project.
put.summary: The store's save of a file of its tree (design 1 §5.3).

post.summary: The manifest reconcile (design 1 §5.5 step 2): the store's tree as its sidecar sees it in, the manifest and the three lists that make the tree match it out.
